The sticky note write is an ordinary obs POST. The frontend sends `POST /obs`, the REST layer saves the obs through `ObsService`, and `HibernateObsDAO` writes the row. I did not read the backend method bodies, so the call chain between them comes from search hits and signatures only.

1. **Frontend sender:** `createStickyNote` in `sticky-note.resource.ts` calls `openmrsFetch` with `POST ${restBaseUrl}/obs`. The body carries `person`, `concept`, `value` and `obsDatetime`. Editing a note uses `updateStickyNote`, which POSTs to `/obs/{uuid}`.
2. **REST handler:** `ObsResource1_8.save(Obs delegate)` in openmrs-module-webservices.rest calls `Context.getObsService().saveObs(delegate, "REST web service")`.
3. **Core service:** `ObsServiceImpl.saveObs(Obs, String)` handles the save. A new obs goes to the private `saveNewOrVoidedObs`, which calls `dao.saveObs(obs)`. `ObsService` declares the interface method.
4. **Data access:** `HibernateObsDAO.saveObs(Obs)` does the database write. `ObsDAO` declares the interface method.
